html:
SMTO-PSM-0017 — SMTO couldn't tell what parameter you want to save

GUID: ae2ab4a3-bfea-4240-89b4-bef8ed2d91f0
Slug: parameter-draft-intent-missing
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • SMTO read your description but couldn't find a clear request to save or update a parameter in it. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Describe the request with the name and the values, for example: "Save a parameter called prod_db with host db1 and port 5432." SMTO needs a name and at least one value to know what to save.
  2. Leave passwords out of the description; add them later on the parameter's Value tab. This keeps secrets out of the request text while still letting SMTO draft the rest.
  3. Or open Parameter Store, select New, fill in Key and the value yourself, and select Save. Creating it directly doesn't depend on SMTO understanding your description.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows a draft parameter you can review, or the parameter appears in the Parameter Store list.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your description (minus any passwords), to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The parameter drafting model response reported is_parameter_request false or returned no draft entries for the prompt.

What this means

  • The structured drafting response says this is not a parameter request or supplies no draft entries. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • The structured drafting response says this is not a parameter request or supplies no draft entries.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the requested parameter intent and returned draft classification without treating it as a saved change.

How to fix it

  • Rephrase the drafting prompt to state the key and the fields to set (for example 'save parameter prod_db with host db1 and port 5432'), or create the entry directly in the Parameter Store editor. Raised by llm_parameter_draft in src/agent_runtime/parameters/drafting.py.
  • Specify which parameter to create or update and its intended nonsecret structure, or use the parameter editor.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A clear intended set/update produces a valid reviewable draft or direct editor input.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
